Name: Jack Lambert
Fun Fact: He played without his two front teeth and once said quarterbacks should wear dresses because of how protected they were becoming
Notes: The face of the Steelers' Steel Curtain defense

Name: Chuck Bednarik
Fun Fact: He was the last two-way player in NFL history - played 60 full minutes of center and linebacker - Concrete Charlie was a different species

Name: Mario Lemieux
Fun Fact: He survived cancer mid-career, came back and scored a goal in his first game back, and then won a second Stanley Cup - the most remarkable comeback in hockey history
Notes: #66 retired by Penguins - played on same line as Jagr #68

Name: Jaromir Jagr
Fun Fact: He chose #68 to honor the Prague Spring of 1968 when Soviet tanks rolled into Czechoslovakia - every time he put on the jersey it meant something political and personal
Notes: Adjacent to Lemieux #66 - two linemates, two Legends

Name: Evgeni Malkin
Fun Fact: In 2009 he became the first Russian to win the Conn Smythe. Won the Hart and Art Ross as regular-season MVP in 2012. Three Cups total. Twenty seasons alongside Crosby probably cost him half his legacy.
Notes: Active legend — review annually

Name: Mean Joe Greene
Fun Fact: The Coca-Cola ad where he gives a kid his jersey made him the most famous defensive player in America - four Super Bowls and the face of the Steel Curtain

Name: Ray Bourque
Fun Fact: He gave up his #7 so Phil Esposito could retire it - wore #77 for the rest of his career - and the whole league cheered when he finally won the Cup in Colorado at 40
Notes: #77 retired by Bruins

Name: Bruce Smith
Fun Fact: The only player in NFL history with 200 career sacks — a record that still stands. 11 Pro Bowls, two Defensive Player of the Year awards, and the anchor of four straight Super Bowl runs in Buffalo.
Notes: #78 retired by Bills

Name: Anthony Muñoz
Stat Label: Pro Bowl Selections (Most Ever at OT)
Fun Fact: 11 straight Pro Bowls, nine first-team All-Pros. Widely considered the greatest offensive tackle in NFL history and the only Bengal inducted as a unanimous first-ballot Hall of Famer.
Notes: #78 retired by Bengals

Name: Jerry Rice
Fun Fact: NFL.com named him the greatest player in NFL history - not the greatest receiver - the greatest player, period - and it's hard to argue

Name: Terrell Owens
Fun Fact: He did situps in his driveway during a public holdout and made it appointment television - one of the most explosive and controversial players in NFL history

Name: Randy Moss
Fun Fact: He ran past defenders so easily in his prime that it looked like they were standing still - the most physically gifted receiver in NFL history
Notes: Note: wore #84 in Minnesota, #81 in New England

Name: Rob Gronkowski
Fun Fact: At 22 he set the single-season TD record for tight ends with 17 — then came out of retirement seven years later to add a fourth Super Bowl ring in Tampa. The most dominant tight end ever.
Notes: First-ballot HOF eligible 2026

Name: Sidney Crosby
Fun Fact: He shot pucks at a dryer in his basement as a kid until the dryer broke - the work ethic behind three Stanley Cups and three Hart Trophies
Notes: ACTIVE - review annually Active legend — review annually.

Name: Tony Gonzalez
Fun Fact: He has 1,325 career receptions - the most by any tight end in NFL history - and redefined what the position could be
Notes: #88 is most HOF-crowded number in NFL history per tier list

Name: Eric Lindros
Fun Fact: He was the most physically dominant player in the NHL in the mid-90s - 6-foot-4 and could skate like a wing - concussions cut short what could have been the greatest career ever

Name: Mike Ditka
Fun Fact: He was the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame - revolutionized the position - and then coached the Bears to the greatest season in NFL history in 1985

Name: Sergei Fedorov
Fun Fact: He became the first Russian player to win the NHL Hart Trophy in 1994 and was known for being able to dominate both offensively and defensively
Notes: One of the greatest two-way forwards in NHL history

Name: Reggie White
Fun Fact: The Minister of Defense - 198 career sacks - a Hall of Famer who combined uncommon physical gifts with genuine religious conviction that he wore openly

Name: Michael Strahan
Fun Fact: He set the single-season sack record with 22.5 in 2001 - and helped the Giants beat the undefeated Patriots in Super Bowl XLII - one of the greatest upsets in NFL history

Name: John Randle
Fun Fact: Undrafted out of Texas A&M-Kingsville, showed up in eye-black war paint and posted 137.5 sacks — the most by a defensive tackle at the time of his retirement.

Name: Connor McDavid
Fun Fact: He skates faster than anyone who has ever played the game - multiple Hart Trophies and Art Ross Trophies - the best player in hockey right now without debate
Notes: ACTIVE - review annually Active legend — review annually.

Name: Wayne Gretzky
Fun Fact: If you remove every goal he ever scored he would still be the all-time points leader just from his assists - #99 was retired across the entire NHL in 1999
Notes: SACRED - retired across all NHL

Name: Aaron Judge
Fun Fact: In 2022 he hit 62 home runs — breaking Roger Maris's AL record that had stood since 1961 — without a single PED allegation. The cleanest power season of the modern era.
Notes: Active legend — review annually

Name: Gilbert Arenas
Fun Fact: He chose #0 because scouts predicted zero minutes at Arizona — then averaged 29 points at his peak. Agent Zero. The gun incident in 2009 cut the era short. He was 27.
Notes: Conduct flag: 2009 locker room gun incident, 50-game suspension. Legacy acknowledged in fun fact — not scrubbed.

Name: Nolan Ryan
Fun Fact: Seven no-hitters — three more than any other pitcher. 5,714 strikeouts, nearly 840 more than anyone else. So dominant that three separate franchises retired his number: the Angels, Astros, and Rangers.

Name: Bobby Hull
Fun Fact: The Golden Jet — led the NHL in goals seven times, 610 career totals. His jump to the WHA in 1972 legitimized the rival league overnight. Three franchises retired his #9: Chicago, Winnipeg, and Phoenix.

Name: Roy Keane
Fun Fact: Dominated Juventus in the 1999 CL semi-final knowing a yellow card meant missing the final. United won. He sat out Barcelona. Ferguson called it the most selfless performance he ever witnessed.

Name: Kenny Dalglish
Fun Fact: Won the English title as both player and Liverpool manager — in 1986 he put himself on at 35 and scored the title-clinching goal at Chelsea. Three European Cups as a player. King Kenny.

Name: Joe Dumars
Fun Fact: Won the 1989 Finals MVP shutting down Michael Jordan, then won it all again the next year. So respected that the NBA named their annual Sportsmanship Award after him while he was still playing.

Name: Johnny Gaudreau
Fun Fact: Johnny Hockey — 115 points in 2021–22, one of the most beloved players of his generation. Killed by a drunk driver in August 2024 at 31. Both Calgary and Columbus retired his #13. The wall holds his number.
Notes: Commemorative entry — retired by both Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets

Name: Mesut Özil
Fun Fact: Wore #10 for Real Madrid, Arsenal, and Germany — then chose #67 at Fenerbahçe because it's the postal prefix for his family's hometown in Turkey. The most thoughtful assist in jersey number history.

Name: Sachin Tendulkar
Fun Fact: Started at #99, switched to #10. After retirement no Indian dared wear it — until Shardul Thakur did in 2017 and was trolled so hard the BCCI quietly retired the number. India's only retired jersey.
Notes: BCCI retired #10 informally in 2017 following public backlash when Shardul Thakur wore it. Two sources on number: thenewsminute.com + india.com/BCCI report.

Name: MS Dhoni
Fun Fact: Born on July 7 — the 7th day of the 7th month — so he wore #7. After he retired, the BCCI officially retired the number in 2023. Only the second Indian player given this honor, after Tendulkar.
Notes: BCCI retired #7 in December 2023 per ddnews.gov.in + espncricinfo.com. Two verified sources.

Name: Virat Kohli
Fun Fact: #18 was a private tribute to a cousin who died young — a detail he kept quiet for years. He also surpassed Tendulkar's record of 49 ODI centuries, becoming the first man to score 50 in the format.
Notes: #18 confirmed at espncricinfo.com ODI shirt numbers + cricketrivalry.com AB de Villiers post confirms Kohli wears 18. 50th ODI century reached 2023/24 — check exact milestone date.

Name: Adam Gilchrist
Fun Fact: Before Gilchrist, keepers batted at the bottom and kept quiet. He averaged 47 in Tests from No. 7 and rewrote what the position could be. Every modern aggressive keeper-batter traces the lineage back to him.
Notes: #18 confirmed: eBay listing for 'Adam Gilchrist 18 Australia One Day Cricket Jersey' + crictoday.com Australian team jersey numbers page + espncricinfo.com ODI shirt numbers article.

Name: Ricky Ponting
Fun Fact: #14 was a tribute to AFL legend Darrel Baldock — a childhood idol he never met. Under Ponting, Australia won 11 straight World Cup matches spanning two tournaments without a loss.
Notes: #14 confirmed at ipl.com Australian cricketers jersey numbers + sportsdunia.com Ponting bio with AFL idol detail.

Name: Shane Warne
Stat Label: Test Wickets (most by a leg-spinner ever)
Fun Fact: His first Ashes ball in 1993 turned three feet and bowled Gatting around his legs — Gatting stared at the pitch, unsure what happened. 'The Ball of the Century.' He died unexpectedly in March 2022, aged 52.
Notes: #23 confirmed: sportskeeda.com Warne/Clarke shirt-number handover story + Etsy/eBay listings for 'Shane Warne 23 Australia One Day Cricket Jersey'. Adds cricket dimension to #23 alongside Jordan/LeBron.

Name: Glenn McGrath
Fun Fact: He predicted scorelines before major matches — often correctly. Before the 2003 World Cup final he predicted a 125-run win. They won by 125 runs. He did it so many times it stopped being surprising.
Notes: #11 confirmed: cricketcountry.com story about Joel Paris 'donning McGrath's No.11 jersey' + zeenews.india.com article both cite McGrath's jersey as 11. Stat note: 'most by a fast bowler at retirement' — James Anderson has since surpassed 563.

Name: Kumar Sangakkara
Fun Fact: At the 2015 World Cup he scored four centuries in four consecutive innings — something no player in the tournament's 40-year history had ever done. He was 37.
Notes: #11 listed as primary number across crictoday.com Sri Lanka jersey page + Quora cricket sources. Secondary number listed as 84. Confidence 4 — single robust source on specific number.

Name: AB de Villiers
Fun Fact: #17 for his birthday, February 17. Fastest ODI fifty (16 balls), century (31 balls), and 150 (62 balls) — all three records from the same innings. When Dewald Brevis wanted the number, he called de Villiers to ask.
Notes: #17 confirmed: quora.com 'Why does AB de Villiers wear #17' + cricketaddictor.com Dewald Brevis/AB de Villiers jersey permission story.

Name: Muttiah Muralitharan
Fun Fact: His 800th wicket came off his very last delivery in Test cricket — planned in advance. He walked off at exactly 800. His Instagram is @murali_800. The number defines him so completely he built his identity around it.
Notes: #8 from crictoday.com Sri Lanka jersey numbers page. Confidence 4 — single source on specific number; 800-wicket stat is universally verified across all cricket databases.

Name: Rohit Sharma
Stat Label: ODI Double Centuries (no one else has two)
Fun Fact: His mother chose #45 because 4+5=9 is auspicious, when #19 was taken at the Under-19 World Cup. He still wears it. His 264 against Sri Lanka in 2014 remains the highest individual score in ODI history.
Notes: #45 confirmed: cricketcountry.com story on how his mother chose the number + cricketliveipl.com. Multiple sources confirm 264 ODI record.

Name: Jasprit Bumrah
Fun Fact: #93 for the year he was born. His bowling action was flagged by coaches throughout his career as one that would break down. They were wrong. Wickets on every continent, ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year for 2024.
Notes: #93 confirmed: cricfevers.com Bumrah jersey number story + bumrah's own quote in newsbytesapp.com ('93 was the year I was born'). Two sources.

Name: Ben Stokes
Fun Fact: A ball deflected off his bat for 4 overthrows in the 2019 World Cup final, gifting England the boundary count that decided it. As Test captain from 2022, 'Bazball' became one of cricket's most entertaining eras.
Notes: #55 confirmed: indiafantasy.com Ben Stokes jersey number article + crictoday.com England jersey numbers page.

Name: Steve Smith
Fun Fact: In his first series back after the sandpaper scandal, he scored 774 Ashes runs — the most dominant performance in 30 years — with a broken arm. His unorthodox technique has sustained a Test average near 60 for over a decade.
Notes: #49 confirmed: auctions.officialmemorabilia.com.au 'Steve Smith #49 Australia 2024/25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy' + crictoday.com Australian jersey numbers page.

Name: Jim Brown
Stat Label: Career Touchdowns (NFL record at retirement; stood 28 years)
Fun Fact: He retired at 30 in 1966 — still in his prime, still the all-time leading rusher — and his rushing record stood for 18 years until Walter Payton broke it. He scored 106 touchdowns in 9 seasons, a record that lasted 28 years until Jerry Rice.
Notes: #32 retired by Browns. HOF 1971 first-ballot. Rushing record (12,312) passed by Payton 10/7/1984; TD record (106) passed by Rice 1994.

Name: Otto Graham
Stat Label: Championship Game Appearances in 10 Pro Seasons
Fun Fact: He led the Browns to the championship game in every single one of his ten pro seasons (1946–1955) — and won seven of them. No quarterback in any era has come close to that. His #14 was the first jersey the Browns ever retired.
Notes: First jersey ever retired by Browns. Originally wore #60, switched to #14 in 1952 when NFL forced linemen into 50–79. HOF 1965.

Name: Lou Groza
Fun Fact: Nicknamed 'The Toe', he was both an offensive tackle and the kicker — and was so synonymous with placekicking that the award given annually to the best college kicker still bears his name.
Notes: #76 retired by Browns. HOF 1974. Lou Groza Award established 1992.

Name: Aaron Donald
Stat Label: NFL Defensive Player of the Year Awards
Fun Fact: He won Defensive Player of the Year three times as an interior tackle — a position that's not supposed to do that — and set the single-season sack record for interior linemen with 20.5 in 2018. He retired with a Super Bowl ring at the top of his game.
Notes: 111 career sacks. SB LVI champion (2021 season). 10x Pro Bowl, 8x All-Pro First Team. DPOY 2017, 2018, 2020. Retired March 2024.

Name: Jerome Bettis
Stat Label: Career Rushing Yards (5th All-Time at Retirement)
Fun Fact: He retired as a Super Bowl champion in his hometown of Detroit — the rare ending where the storybook actually wrote itself. He left the game 5th on the all-time rushing list and was nicknamed 'The Bus' because tacklers bounced off him.
Notes: #36 not officially retired by Steelers but not reissued. HOF 2015. 6x Pro Bowler. Won SB XL in his final game (Feb 2006).

Name: Eddie George
Fun Fact: He won the Heisman at Ohio State and then never missed a game in his nine NFL seasons — 130 straight starts in a sport where running backs typically break down. He carried the Titans to the Super Bowl in 1999, finishing one yard short on the final play.
Notes: #27 retired by Titans 2019. Heisman 1995. College HOF 2011. NFL HOF semifinalist but not inducted.

Name: J.J. Watt
Stat Label: NFL Defensive Player of the Year Awards (Tied for Most Ever)
Fun Fact: He won Defensive Player of the Year three times in four years (2012, 2014, 2015) — a feat only Lawrence Taylor matches. He never won a championship but was so dominant in Houston that the city built its sports identity around him.
Notes: 114.5 career sacks. 101.0 with Texans (franchise record). Houston Sports HOF Class of 2026. HOF-eligible 2028.

Name: Sócrates
Stat Label: Captain of the Greatest Team Never to Win a World Cup
Fun Fact: He captained Brazil's 1982 World Cup squad — the most beloved team in football history that never won the trophy — while simultaneously practicing medicine and leading the Corinthians Democracy movement against the military dictatorship. They called him Doctor Sócrates and he earned both halves.
Notes: Wore #8 for Corinthians and Brazil. Trained medical doctor. Died 2011.

Name: Sergio Busquets
Fun Fact: He won three Champions Leagues and nine La Ligas as the holding midfielder for the Guardiola era — the player Xavi said 'plays in tomorrow, while everyone else is in today.' Add a World Cup and a Euros and he's won more than almost anyone alive.
Notes: 9 La Liga + 7 Copa del Rey + 3 Champions League at Barça. 2010 World Cup + Euro 2012 with Spain. 143 Spain caps.

Name: Wesley Sneijder
Fun Fact: His 2010 season was the closest anyone has come to a perfect calendar year in football — Serie A, Champions League, Coppa Italia and the Club World Cup with Inter, then runner-up at the World Cup with the Netherlands. He should have won the Ballon d'Or.
Notes: Wore #10 at Inter Milan (NOT Galatasaray — wore #14 there). UEFA Midfielder of Season 2010. Originally suggested at Galatasaray; corrected to Inter.

Name: Henrik Larsson
Fun Fact: He scored 242 goals in 313 games for Celtic, walking out to the Magnificent Seven theme tune — Celtic fans called him the King of Kings. In his last match for Barcelona he set up both goals to win the 2006 Champions League final off the bench.
Notes: 4 Scottish Premier League titles with Celtic. 2006 UCL winner with Barcelona (sub).

Name: Kawhi Leonard
Stat Label: Finals MVPs with Different Teams (2014 Spurs, 2019 Raptors)
Fun Fact: He's one of only four players in NBA history to win Finals MVP with two different teams — taking down LeBron's Heat with the Spurs in 2014, then dragging Toronto to its first championship in 2019. The most efficient two-way superstar of the modern era.
Notes: Active legend — review annually. Wore #2 at Spurs, Raptors, and Clippers. 2x DPOY (2015, 2016) — first non-center back-to-back since Rodman. 7x All-Star.

Name: Yao Ming
Fun Fact: He broke Michael Jordan's All-Star vote record in 2005 — 2,558,278 votes, because a billion Chinese fans suddenly had an NBA player to vote for. He opened the league to a whole continent and made the Hall of Fame in nine injury-shortened seasons.
Notes: #11 retired by Rockets 2/3/2017. HOF 2016 — first Chinese national inducted. #1 overall pick 2002. 8x All-Star, 5x All-NBA.

Name: Marc-André Fleury
Fun Fact: He retired with 575 wins — the most in NHL history by anyone not named Martin Brodeur — across three Stanley Cup runs in Pittsburgh and a Vezina Trophy at age 36 in Las Vegas. The most beloved goalie of his generation, in two different cities.
Notes: 3 Stanley Cups (2009, 2016, 2017). Vezina Trophy 2021. Jennings Trophy 2021. 375 wins with Penguins (franchise record).

Name: Edgar Martinez
Stat Label: DH Award Renamed in His Honor (2004)
Fun Fact: Major League Baseball renamed the Outstanding Designated Hitter Award after him on his retirement day in 2004 — the rarest of honors, given to a player whose dominance redefined a position. He spent all 18 of his pro seasons in Seattle and made the Hall of Fame in 2019 on the strength of being the greatest pure hitter of his era.
Notes: HOF 2019 (85.4% of BBWAA vote). #11 retired by Mariners Aug 12, 2017. 7x All-Star, 5x Silver Slugger, 2x batting title.

Name: Adrian Peterson
Stat Label: Rushing Yards, 2012 MVP Season (Return from Torn ACL)
Fun Fact: He tore his ACL and MCL in December 2011 — an injury that ends most careers — and came back to rush for 2,097 yards and win MVP in the same season. He also holds the single-game rushing record at 296 yards. The most physically dominant back to ever play the position.
Notes: #28 retired by Vikings November 2023. Conduct flag: 2014 child abuse charges, served suspension, reinstated. 2012 AP MVP, 7x Pro Bowl, 4x rushing title. HOF eligible 2027. Source 1: pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01.htm. Source 2: vikings.com retired numbers.

Name: Curt Schilling
Stat Label: World Series Rings (1993 PHI, 2001 ARI, 2004 BOS, 2007 BOS)
Fun Fact: He pitched Game 6 of the 2004 ALCS with a ruptured tendon sutured directly to his ankle skin — the bloody sock game — went 6 innings, gave up 1 run, and sent the Red Sox to the World Series. He removed himself from the HOF ballot. The wall holds the number.
Notes: CONDITIONAL: 216 career wins, 3116 Ks, 4 WS rings. Removed himself from HOF ballot 2022; never inducted. Source 1: baseball-reference.com/players/s/schilcu01.htm. Source 2: MLB.com postseason records.

Name: Jason Kelce
Fun Fact: He retired as the most decorated center in NFL history. His Super Bowl parade speech — delivered in a Mummer's costume — went viral instantly and might be the greatest victory speech in American sports.
Notes: #62 retired by Eagles 2025. Retired March 2024, HOF eligible 2029 (5-year rule). 6x Pro Bowl, Super Bowl LII champion. Source 1: pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KelcJa00.htm. Source 2: philadelphiaeagles.com retired numbers.

Name: Joe Thornton
Fun Fact: He won the Hart Trophy and Art Ross Trophy in 2006 — but had been traded mid-season from Boston to San Jose. The league gave him both awards spanning two cities. He finished with 96 points in just 58 games with the Sharks alone.
Notes: #19 retired by Sharks 2022. HOF inducted June 2025 (Class of 2025). Hart + Art Ross 2006. Source 1: hockey-reference.com/players/t/thornjo01.html. Source 2: nhl.com/sharks/team/retired-numbers.

Name: Champ Bailey
Stat Label: Pro Bowl Selections (NFL Record for a Cornerback)
Fun Fact: For the better part of a decade, he was so dominant that entire halves of the field were effectively removed from the game — quarterbacks simply stopped throwing his way. Twelve Pro Bowls, the most ever at cornerback. He never won a ring, but his HOF case needed no championship.
Notes: #24 retired by Broncos 2019. HOF inducted 2019. 12 Pro Bowls (record for CB). SB XLVIII with Denver (lost 43-8). Denver won SB50 in Feb 2016, 21 months after Bailey retired Oct 2014 — no ring. Source 1: pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BailCh00.htm. Source 2: broncos.com retired numbers.

Name: Marvin Harrison
Stat Label: Receptions in 2002 (NFL Record at the Time)
Fun Fact: He and Peyton Manning connected so often and so precisely that they became the blueprint for every pocket passer and possession receiver that followed. His 143 catches in 2002 set the NFL record — broken by Michael Thomas (149) in 2019. The quietest superstar the league ever produced.
Notes: #88 retired by Colts 2016. HOF 2016 (first ballot). 8x Pro Bowl. 143 receptions (2002) was NFL record at the time — surpassed by Michael Thomas (149) in 2019. Source 1: pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HarrMa00.htm. Source 2: colts.com retired numbers.

Name: Chris Paul
Fun Fact: Every basketball mind agrees: no one has ever run a pick-and-roll more efficiently, orchestrated a half-court set more precisely, or defended a point guard more ruthlessly. He retired in 2026 holding the all-time records for both assists and steals.
Notes: #3 worn throughout career. Retired end of 2025-26 season. 12x All-Star, 12x All-NBA, ROY 2006. All-time assists leader (passed Stockton 2023). All-time steals leader. Source 1: basketball-reference.com/players/p/paulch01.html. Source 2: nba.com/player/101108.

Name: Luka Dončić
Stat Label: Points in a Single Game (January 2024, 3rd Most in NBA History)
Fun Fact: He wore #7 at Real Madrid and doubled it to #77 in the NBA. At 22 he was already dribbling through defenses like they belonged to a different sport. Traded to the Lakers in January 2025 after the Mavericks lost the 2024 Finals to Boston in 5 games.
Notes: Active legend — review annually. #77 worn at Real Madrid and throughout NBA career. Traded to Lakers January 2025. Mavericks lost 2024 Finals to Boston Celtics in 5 games. 2024 NBA MVP. Source 1: basketball-reference.com/players/d/doncilu01.html. Source 2: nba.com/player/1629029.

Name: Trent Alexander-Arnold
Stat Label: Premier League Assists, 2019-20 (Most Ever by a Defender)
Fun Fact: His quick corner to Origi in the 2019 UCL semi-final second leg turned a dead Liverpool attack into a miracle comeback against Barcelona. He redefined what a right back could be — 13 assists in one PL season is more than most midfielders manage.
Notes: Active legend — review annually. #66 at Liverpool. Moved to Real Madrid on free transfer summer 2025. UCL winner 2019, PL winner 2019-20. Sits alongside Mario Lemieux at #66. Source 1: fbref.com/en/players/32a3d09f/Trent-Alexander-Arnold. Source 2: premierleague.com player stats.

Name: Luis Suárez
Stat Label: Premier League Goals in 2013-14 (Golden Boot; 31 in 33 Games)
Fun Fact: In 2013-14 he scored 31 Premier League goals in 33 games and nearly dragged Liverpool to their first title in 24 years. A year later he won the treble with Barcelona. Three biting incidents are on his record; the wall notes them and moves on — the goals happened.
Notes: Conduct flag: 3 biting incidents (Chiellini 2014 WC, Ivanovic 2013, Bakkal 2010); Evra racism charge 2011. Retired 2025. 2014 WC Golden Boot. Source 1: transfermarkt.com/luis-suarez/profil. Source 2: fbref.com/en/players/e7f4a38d/Luis-Suarez.

Name: Gwyneth Phillips
Stat Label: Playoff Save Percentage, PWHL 2024 (Ilana Kloss Playoff MVP)
Fun Fact: In the inaugural PWHL playoffs she stopped shots at a .952 clip and won the Ilana Kloss Playoff MVP — the first of its kind. PWHL got its own set of legends from Day 1. The wall adds its first.
Notes: CONDITIONAL — PWHL is a growing league, recognition still building. #1 confirmed goaltender number. Active legend — review annually. Source 1: pwhl.com player profile + playoff stats. Source 2: PWHL official Ilana Kloss MVP Award announcement (2024).

Name: LaDainian Tomlinson
Fun Fact: In 2006 he set the NFL records for most touchdowns in a season (31), most rushing touchdowns (28), and most points scored (186) — all in the same campaign. He won MVP so decisively the vote wasn't close. The most complete offensive season by a running back in NFL history.
Notes: #21 retired by Chargers 2009. HOF 2017. 2006 AP MVP. Source 1: pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TomlLa00.htm. Source 2: chargers.com/history/retired-numbers.

Name: Drew Brees
Stat Label: Career Passing Yards (NFL All-Time Record at Retirement)
Fun Fact: He rebuilt his shoulder after a devastating injury in 2005, chose New Orleans over Miami, and spent 15 years rewriting the record books while helping a devastated city rebuild its identity. Super Bowl XLIV. His 80,358 career passing yards were the all-time NFL record at retirement.
Notes: #9 retired by Saints 2022. HOF 2024. Super Bowl XLIV. 80,358 career passing yards (record at retirement — surpassed by Tom Brady). Source 1: pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BreeDr00.htm. Source 2: neworleanssaints.com/history/retired-numbers.

Name: Iker Casillas
Fun Fact: He won three Champions Leagues, two Euros, and a World Cup with Spain — and after the 2010 World Cup final he kissed his then-girlfriend Sara Carbonero live on air while she was reporting for Spanish TV on the pitch. Saint Iker. The most decorated Spanish footballer of his era.
Notes: #1 worn throughout career at Real Madrid and Porto. 3x UCL (2000, 2002, 2014). 2010 World Cup, Euro 2008, Euro 2012 with Spain. Source 1: transfermarkt.com/iker-casillas/profil. Source 2: realmadrid.com legends profile.

Name: Kaká
Stat Label: Ballon d'Or (Last Winner Before the Messi-Ronaldo Decade)
Fun Fact: He won the 2007 Ballon d'Or and then Messi won every one that followed for the next five years, and Ronaldo after that, and Messi again. Kaká is the last player before the GOAT debate to win the thing — making his the final Ballon d'Or of a different era of football.
Notes: Wore #22 at AC Milan, #8 at Real Madrid. Anchored at #22 (AC Milan peak). 2007 Ballon d'Or, 2007 UCL, 2002 World Cup with Brazil. Source 1: transfermarkt.com/kaka/profil. Source 2: acmilan.com legends profile.

Name: Sergio Ramos
Fun Fact: He scored in the 93rd minute of the 2014 Champions League final to force extra time against Atlético Madrid — one of the most dramatic headers in football history. Four Champions Leagues, a World Cup, two Euros. He spent 16 years at Real Madrid and won everything.
Notes: #4 worn at Real Madrid throughout career. 4x UCL (2014, 2016, 2017, 2018). 2010 World Cup, Euro 2008, Euro 2012 with Spain. Most international caps by a European player at retirement. Source 1: transfermarkt.com/sergio-ramos/profil. Source 2: realmadrid.com legends profile.

Name: Steven Gerrard
Fun Fact: Down 3-0 to AC Milan at half-time in the 2005 Champions League final, Gerrard headed Liverpool's first goal, sparked a comeback for the ages, and lifted the trophy. He spent 17 years at Liverpool and never won the Premier League — the title slipped in 2014 when he famously slipped against Chelsea. He never left.
Notes: #8 worn throughout career at Liverpool. 1x UCL (Istanbul 2005). Never won Premier League. Source 1: fbref.com/en/players/18a10664/Steven-Gerrard. Source 2: liverpoolfc.com/history/past-players/steven-gerrard.

Name: Alessandro Del Piero
Fun Fact: He spent 19 years at Juventus, scored 290 goals to become their all-time scorer, and when the club was relegated for match-fixing in 2006, he stayed. He went to Serie B with them. He won the World Cup that same summer and came back down with the club he loved.
Notes: #10 worn throughout Juventus career (1993-2012). 290 goals — Juventus all-time record. 2006 World Cup with Italy. 1996 UCL winner. Source 1: transfermarkt.com/alessandro-del-piero/profil. Source 2: juventus.com legends profile.

Name: Robert Lewandowski
Stat Label: Bundesliga Goals in 2020-21 (Breaking Gerd Müller's 49-Year Record)
Fun Fact: He scored 41 Bundesliga goals in 2020-21, breaking Gerd Müller's 49-year-old record, and still didn't win the Ballon d'Or — the ceremony was cancelled in 2020 and Messi won in 2021. Most football people think he was robbed of at least one. The greatest striker of his generation.
Notes: Active legend — review annually. #9 worn at Bayern Munich and FC Barcelona. 2021 FIFA Best Men's Player. 2020 UCL winner. Source 1: transfermarkt.com/robert-lewandowski/profil. Source 2: fbref.com/en/players/8d78e732/Robert-Lewandowski.

Name: Virgil van Dijk

Name: Don Hutson
